overall_explanation: No P0 defects found. I checked the new fleet store and commit adapter, recovery codec and replay, capability gating on lease acquire and renew, the pin integration, startup ownership rebinding, the scheduler and retention changes, and the removal of the Intel Mac build target. Removing darwin/amd64 is consistent across GoReleaser, the Homebrew cask guard, CI matrices, the release verification script, and the publisher's required checks. Replay now uses the retained baseline before it compares compatibility, so binary upgrades no longer deadlock. Capability failures return conflicts, and a runtime that cannot replay the shared publication stays a follower and never requests the lease. Two narrower concerns do not meet the P0 threshold and were left out. First, stricter renewal-identity checks could affect existing standalone lease adapters that return incomplete lease records. Second, the cask depends on `depends_on` being valid inside an `on_macos` block.
